findings.title: Limit and cap accept fractional strings and unchecked overflow because IsNumeric is not whole-number validation
evidence: Engine/Source/Runtime/Core/Public/Misc/CString.h:148-175: IsNumeric accepts an optional sign and at most one dot.
CString.h:1219-1222: Atoi delegates to the platform conversion; no whole-string or overflow check is performed.
TurboMCPCallLogTools.cpp:53-67 and TurboMCPCallCostTools.cpp:126-144 call IsNumeric then Atoi.
findings.observed_source_behavior: 1.5 passes IsNumeric and Atoi converts the integer prefix to 1; +5 is accepted as a positive integer spelling and is a compatibility policy choice, not inherently malformed; 1e3 and 1..2 are refused. Overflow behavior is platform/CRT-dependent and was not executed.
findings.existing_assertions: Tools/test-call-log.py:400-408 and Tools/test-call-cost.py:344-353 assert only banana and zero; no fractional, signed-positive or overflow case.

findings.title: Empty-log return precedes cap validation only in ReadTurboMCPCallCost
evidence: TurboMCPCallCostTools.cpp:104-116 returns the empty-log report before the cap block at :126-145.
TurboMCPCallLogTools.cpp:53-69 validates Limit before it reads or filters entries.
findings.observed_source_behavior: With no entries in memory, ReadTurboMCPCallCost(cap=banana) or cap=0 returns the empty report, while ReadTurboMCPCallLog(limit=banana or 0) returns an error. The two readers apply different precedence to the same request shape.
findings.existing_assertions: Invalid caps are tested only with populated logs; no empty-log invalid-cap case exists.

findings.title: Truncation continuation tells the caller to use since=newest, which cannot fetch the omitted older records
evidence: TurboMCPCallLogTools.cpp:104-110 reverses the selected list newest-first and cuts to Cap.
TurboMCPCallLogTools.cpp:79 excludes Entry.Timestamp <= SinceText; since is a later-than bound.
TurboMCPCallLogTools.cpp:185-189 prints 'pass since=<Selected[0].Timestamp> to page forward' when Total > Selected.
findings.observed_source_behavior: The omitted records are older than the newest shown. Passing the echoed newest timestamp selects only records later than it, not the omitted older records; the advice cannot retrieve what it says it will.
findings.existing_assertions: Tools/test-call-log.py:262-280 proves since excludes older entries; it does not exercise the Total > Selected continuation path.

findings.title: These four plain-FString tools carry no ARC02 result line, but call_structured treats every TurboMCP.* toolset as migrated
evidence: None of the four implementations calls FTurboMCPResult::AppendTo. The only production caller is TurboMCPGraphRepointTools.cpp:27.
Tools/tmcp.py:422-431 defaults requires_result=True when toolset starts with TurboMCP.
Existing engine suites use Session.call (compatibility text), not call_structured.
findings.observed_source_behavior: A call_structured invocation without requires_result=False raises ResultProtocolError for these four, while Session.call succeeds. Whether these four should be migrated or explicitly compatibility-only is a policy decision; this checkpoint does not choose it.
findings.existing_assertions: test-result-contract.py covers GraphRepoint and a native tool, not these four. It passes, but that does not prove their structured path.

findings.title: Switching the log OFF leaves its own start record with no end
evidence: FScopedCall writes start in its constructor only if Write sees logging enabled (TurboMCPCallLog.cpp:254-270; Write gate at :216-221).
Finish writes the end through Write, which is gated by the setting (TurboMCPCallLog.cpp:272-305).
EditTurboMCPCallLog sets bEnableCallLog=false at TurboMCPCallLogTools.cpp:227 before returning at :237-247.
findings.observed_source_behavior: ON->OFF: start is written, body disables logging, end is suppressed. The in-memory/log file record is a start-only call, which the timeline intentionally renders as running/missing-end and which looks like a crash. ON->OFF also persists the setting. OFF->ON: no start, but the end is written after enabling; unchanged states produce a pair when already ON and nothing when already OFF.
findings.existing_assertions: Tools/test-call-log.py exercises off/on transitions but does not assert the record shape after switching OFF.

findings.title: Domain refusals are successful reflected values, so the recorder logs bError=false and failed-call counts omit them
evidence: FFunctionLibraryToolset::ExecuteToolInternal returns MakeValue(JsonToString(ResultValue)) for a normal reflected return and MakeError only for unknown tool/toolset, script exception, conversion failure or invalid result (FunctionLibraryToolset.cpp:134-197).

ObjectFunctionToolCall.cpp:461-500 converts a normal FString return through PropertyToJsonData; :502-521 wraps it in returnValue; required-param and conversion failures are MakeError before invocation (:105-162, :390-413).
TurboMCPCallRecorder.cpp:126-128 sets bError = Result.HasError(); FScopedCall stores only that boolean (TurboMCPCallLog.cpp:272-305).
ReadTurboMCPCallCost counts bError at :237-240; ReadTurboMCPCallLog's filter maps bError to 'error'/'ok' at :95.
findings.observed_source_behavior: Ordinary error-prefixed FString refusals are reflected as successful values. When recorded, their plugin end has bError=false and does not contribute to error-flag-based failed counts. The error-status filter branch does not match it, but other OR branches can match tool/source/argument text containing error. An error returned by the inner invocation after the recorder starts produces bError=true if logging remains enabled. Failures before wrapper entry or transport disconnects do not guarantee such a record.

controls.ordinary_refusal: EditTurboMCPCallLog enabled=banana returns 'error: ... is not a yes or no' from the body.
controls.genuine_invocation_error: With logging enabled and the recorder installed on an enabled toolset, invoke the known EditTurboMCPCallLog tool with its required Enabled field omitted. Verify the request reaches the wrapper, then fails inner required-parameter validation before the body. A disabled/filtered toolset or transport failure is not an equivalent control.

findings.existing_assertions: Tools/test-call-log.py:386-397 checks the bad-boolean text but not the log record's bError or the cost failed count; no invocation-error control asserts bError=true.
findings.repair_note: No prose parser is proposed. A production repair must use a structured domain outcome (for example an ARC02 result line) or an engine-provided structured error; this checkpoint only adds the probe requirement.

findings.title: Tool help omits requiredness and defaults that the schema actually prints
evidence: docs/design/protocol.md:13 requires help to state parameter meaning, requiredness, accepted formats, side effects and a valid example.
TurboMCPAgentHelp.cpp:461-493 prints only name:type-description from properties; it never reads inputSchema.required and never prints a default.
TurboMCPToolSchema.cpp:127-140 reads the required array; :701-719 prints REQUIRED and default= for each parameter.
TurboMCPToolsets.h:105-109 claims both help parameters are required 'whatever its default'; JsonSchemaGenerator.cpp:288-299 requires non-optional parameters without defaults, not every FString.
findings.observed_source_behavior: Help for a tool with a required parameter prints the same shape as an optional one. The schema reader distinguishes them. The header's reason for requiredness is stale even though these two parameters are in fact required because they have no defaults.
findings.existing_assertions: test-agent-help.py checks only 'parameters:' and the 2000-character bound; no REQUIRED/default assertion.

findings.title: Help single-tool 2000-character promise is only a warning; summary has no character cap
evidence: TurboMCPToolsets.h:102-103 says the reply stays under 2000 characters for one tool; that declaration belongs to ReadTurboMCPToolHelp.
TurboMCPAgentHelp.cpp:536-542 is reached only on the single-tool path and appends a warning; it does not cut the text.
TurboMCPAgentHelp.cpp:385-430 is the summary path: it returns before the budget check, and MaxSummaryTools=12 is a row cap, not a character cap.
TurboMCPToolsets.h:481 is the separate ReadTurboMCPToolSchema declaration; its 2000-character cap is not evidence for help.
TurboMCPToolSchema.cpp:783-789 implements the schema tool's separate hard cut.
findings.observed_source_behavior: A single tool's help can exceed 2000 characters and is returned whole with a warning. A summary can also exceed 2000 characters but is limited only to 12 rows and returned before the warning. The schema reader's single-tool branch is the one that cuts at 2000 and announces the cut. These are three different behaviors.
findings.existing_assertions: test-agent-help.py:63-65 checks <=2000 only for selected short single-tool help; it has no long single-tool, long summary or schema-cut assertion.

findings.title: Status is declared free of cost/effects but the recorder can write and rotate the log
evidence: TurboMCPToolsets.h:64-66 says the status tool costs nothing and changes nothing.
TurboMCPCallRecorder.cpp:103-130 wraps every toolset and creates FScopedCall before forwarding.
TurboMCPCallLog.cpp:216-234 writes only when logging is enabled; :254-305 writes start/end, and AppendToFile can rotate at 4 MiB.
findings.observed_source_behavior: When call logging is ON, a status call appends a start and end record and can rotate the log. When logging is OFF, it has no log side effect. The declaration's absolute claim is false in the ON state.
findings.existing_assertions: No test checks status's log side effect; call-log tests use status as an ordinary recorded call.

findings.title: Status reports declared and registered layers but not enabled or discoverable ones
evidence: TurboMCPToolsets.cpp:36-43 is the static declared-class list; :184 prints its size as 'N toolsets'.

TurboMCPToolsets.cpp:133-148 uses UToolsetRegistry::IsToolsetClassRegistered for each class; IsToolsetClassRegistered returns true for a handler-map entry even when the toolset is disabled (UToolsetRegistry.cpp:91-106).

FToolset::GetJsonSchema returns empty for a disabled toolset (Toolset.cpp:115-120), and GetToolsetJsonSchemas skips empty schemas (ToolsetRegistry.cpp:231-245); help/schema therefore omit a disabled toolset.
DescribeServerState checks the module/server pointer and reports settings, not listening or client discovery (TurboMCPToolsets.cpp:94-130).
findings.observed_source_behavior: Status can print 'registered:' for a disabled toolset that help/schema cannot see, and always prints the declared class count as 'N toolsets'. If the registry subsystem is unavailable, all classes print MISSING without a separate registry-unavailable sentence.
findings.existing_assertions: No test distinguishes declared/registered/enabled/schema-listed/discoverable counts or checks a disabled toolset.

evidence: TurboMCPToolSchema.cpp:291-323 normalizes case, spaces, underscores, brackets, angle brackets and hyphens; :474-533 accepts exact/short-tail/suffix toolset forms; :561-570 accepts bare or published full tool names.
TurboMCPAgentHelp.cpp:378-383 accepts exact full or dotted-suffix toolset names only; :449-450 matches only the bare tool name.

No help test covers 'Read', normalized variants, qualified ToolName, empty ToolsetName + tool, or ambiguous suffix matches.

findings.title: Help does not distinguish a missing schema/properties object from a zero-parameter tool
evidence: TurboMCPAgentHelp.cpp:461-503: a missing inputSchema skips the whole parameter block; a present inputSchema without properties prints 'parameters: none'; a zero-parameter tool prints 'parameters: 0 (this tool takes no parameters)'.
TurboMCPToolSchema.cpp:207-213 records OddSchemaNote for missing inputSchema/properties, and :694-699 prints that note; :701 prints the parameter count.
findings.observed_source_behavior: A missing inputSchema produces no parameter section at all; an inputSchema without a properties object produces 'parameters: none'; a real zero-parameter tool with an empty properties object produces 'parameters: 0 (this tool takes no parameters)'. The schema reader records OddSchemaNote for the missing cases.
findings.existing_assertions: No test supplies a schema without inputSchema or checks the difference from a zero-parameter tool.

findings.title: ForceUpdate does not establish refresh success; pinned Perforce can return cached state with Succeeded
evidence: TurboMCPSourceControl.cpp:293 calls Provider.GetState(Row.File, EStateCacheUsage::ForceUpdate) for every resolved file.

ISourceControlProvider.cpp:50-60 implements the single-file helper by calling the array GetState and returning only a nonempty state when the array call returns Succeeded; TurboMCP never receives the refresh result.
PerforceSourceControlProvider.cpp:423-433 executes FUpdateStatus on ForceUpdate but ignores its result, fetches GetStateInternal from StateCache, and returns ECommandResult::Succeeded.
PerforceSourceControlProvider.cpp:131-151 creates a cached DontCare state for a filename absent from the cache; PerforceSourceControlState.h:52-56 defaults it to DontCare.
R13 already records the limit: docs/audit/native-overlap.md:35,88 and docs/audit/technical-debt.md:52-53.
findings.observed_source_behavior: A provider can return a cached or unknown state after a failed refresh and still report Succeeded. TurboMCP reports the state as if it were a current measurement. This is a provider-diagnostic answer, not stale-proof freshness evidence.
findings.existing_assertions: test-vcs.py has no failed-refresh/cached-state case; Perforce is only tested when IsAvailable() is false, and Git is a no-op provider.

findings.title: A non-null provider state is never checked with IsUnknown(); Perforce DontCare can be reported as source-controlled
evidence: TurboMCPSourceControl.cpp:295-317 treats any non-null state as measured and reads IsSourceControlled/IsCheckedOut/IsAdded/IsCurrent/IsModified/IsIgnored/CanCheckout.
ISourceControlState.h:208 exposes IsUnknown(); TurboMCP never calls it.
PerforceSourceControlState.cpp:356-359 returns true for DontCare; PerforceSourceControlState.cpp:326-329 returns IsSourceControlled true for DontCare as well.
PerforceSourceControlState.cpp:168-206 displays DontCare as 'Unknown', but the structured flags are still printed as measured booleans.
findings.observed_source_behavior: The null-state branch is handled, but a non-null unknown state is not: Perforce's default DontCare state can print under source control: true, checked out: false, current: false and provider text Unknown. The output does not say the state is unknown.
findings.existing_assertions: No test creates a non-null IsUnknown state; test-vcs.py only exercises the null/no-provider and Git/Perforce-unavailable cases.

findings.title: Duplicate asset inputs are preserved, producing duplicate rows, state queries and checkout attempts
evidence: TurboMCPAssetResolver.cpp:182-206 SplitList splits on comma/pipe, trims and culls empty parts, but never deduplicates.
TurboMCPSourceControl.cpp:252-320 loops every input and creates one row/GetState call per duplicate.
TurboMCPSourceControl.cpp:443-527 Checkout loops every row and can issue FCheckOut once per duplicate.
TurboMCPSourceControl.cpp:390-404 prints assets: N and one 1-based row per input, so duplicates inflate the count.
findings.observed_source_behavior: Passing the same resolved asset twice produces two rows; with a provider it produces two GetState(ForceUpdate) calls and can issue two FCheckOut operations for one file. No duplicate warning or deduplication exists. Ordering is preserved and empty separators are silently culled.
findings.existing_assertions: test-vcs.py uses exactly two distinct fixtures and checks len(rows)==2; it never sends a duplicate or separator-only input.

findings.title: Checkout executes against the plan state without revalidation, post-operation read-back or aggregate outcome
evidence: TurboMCPSourceControl.cpp:293 reads state once; Checkout at :410-530 never calls GetState before or after Provider.Execute.
Checkout decides to skip from plan fields bCheckedOut/bAdded/bStateRead/CanCheckout (:455-488) and then executes FCheckOut at :491-492; it does not recheck the file, provider, enablement or state.

The result section (:494-522) reports the operation's ECommandResult and messages only. The result fields bAttempted/bSucceeded/ProviderAnswer in TurboMCPSourceControl.h:101-109 are not populated by this path.
The per-asset loop continues after failures; there is no rollback, aggregate count or partial-success summary.
Preview and Edit each call Plan separately (:39-50); sharing the Plan function does not share a state snapshot across calls, so state changes between calls can change the answer.
findings.observed_source_behavior: A stale plan can skip a file that is no longer checked out/added, or attempt a checkout on a file that has changed owner/state. ECommandResult::Succeeded is reported as the provider's operation result, not as a verified checkout; no post-state read proves the lock. A multi-asset call can partially succeed, with per-row results but no aggregate or rollback.
findings.existing_assertions: test-vcs.py only exercises Git no-op and no-provider/Perforce-unavailable paths; it never observes a successful checkout or reads state back. test-vcs-write.py tests write tools, not this checkout tool.

findings.title: Checked-out-by-other, non-null unknown and read-only distinctions are not surfaced as structured state
evidence: TurboMCPSourceControl.cpp:309-317 calls IsSourceControlled/IsCheckedOut/IsAdded/IsCurrent/IsModified/IsIgnored/CanCheckout but not IsCheckedOutOther or IsUnknown.
TurboMCPSourceControl.cpp:134-142 prints those seven flags plus a CanCheckout flag; checked-out-other and unknown appear only if the provider's own display text mentions them.
ISourceControlState.h:156 exposes IsCheckedOutOther; :208 exposes IsUnknown.
The plan prints UsesLocalReadOnlyState at :238,363 but does not inspect a file's read-only attribute; CanCheckout is the only structured read-only-adjacent signal.
findings.observed_source_behavior: Read/Preview state rows cannot distinguish checked out by another user, a genuinely unknown non-null state, or a filesystem read-only asset except through provider text or CanCheckout. The declaration says it reports 'whether it is checked out here', which is true, but the broader state question is not structured.
findings.existing_assertions: test-vcs.py does not assert checked-out-other, unknown-state or read-only flags; the Git assertions only require checked-out/out-of-date lines to exist.

repairs.negative_control: Valid 1 and, if the policy preserves it, +1 still return one bounded row without an error.

No pagination or schema change is part of this repair.

repairs.rollback: Revert the log tool and test file only.

preserved_behavior: OFF means no new start/end records
normal ON calls keep start/end pairs
crash evidence for genuinely unfinished calls
repairs.synthetic_probe: With logging ON, call EditTurboMCPCallLog(enabled=false), then read the log with logging OFF; inspect the last record phases and the timeline; repeat ON->ON, OFF->OFF and OFF->ON.

Proposed policy: write an end only when a start was written for that call; a call that started OFF remains unrecorded even if logging is enabled during it. This preserves normal OFF suppression and never authorizes writes after disable except closing a start that was already written. A header/state field may be required; that is an unresolved scope item, not permission to edit the header in this checkpoint.

schema_validation.finding: The four C++ signatures have no defaults. FJsonSchemaGenerator marks non-optional function parameters without defaults as required; ObjectFunctionToolCall checks required fields and fills schema defaults before invoking. Therefore an omitted field is rejected before the body, while an explicit empty string reaches the body and selects the documented in-code default/refusal. This is a source trace, not a live schema call.
